description:
The fixed-probability random P/D CONTROL arm. Specification of record: algorithms/random_disagg.go. Not a transfer: it has no simulated counterpart and no sim_results/ entry (R1), so it supports arm-vs-arm claims on the target and no sim-vs-real claim. It exists to be beaten -- run at the focal arm's own realized disaggregation rate, it separates WHICH requests are disaggregated from HOW MANY, which no other arm-vs-baseline comparison in this bundle does.

IT ENTERED THIS TRANSLATION BY `sim2real translation append`, NOT BY /sim2real-translate. Consequences, both real: translation_output.json records source_path = null and source_sha256 = null for appended arms, so nothing machine-links the running image to the specification (R5); and the plugin was hand-written rather than generated, which is why it is NOT listed under transfer.yaml:algorithms -- a future `sim2real translate --force` would regenerate it as a PICKER, and this arm is a DECIDER. See the transfer.yaml comment.

THIS MANIFEST EXISTS SO THE TRANSLATION IS COMPLETE FOR ALL THREE ARMS. Without it, `sim2real build --translation pdinfocomm3` fails its completeness check (sim2real.py:2245-2257) for EVERY arm, not just this one, because the check requires generated/<algo>/<algo>_output.json to exist for each entry in algorithms[]. With it, this arm rebuilds through the normal overlay path like the other two -- which also restores --force-rebuild for it, something `sim2real translation append` has no flag for.

THE MANIFEST IS DELIBERATELY NOT A UNION, unlike the other two arms'. Theirs declare a 35-path union because they SHARE one Go package and one registration file, so neither arm's subset compiles alone. This arm shares no package with them: its decider lives in the target's own `disagg` package, and that is FORCED rather than chosen -- the deciderPlugin interface and its disaggregate method are UNEXPORTED (pkg/epp/framework/plugins/scheduling/profilehandler/disagg/decider_plugin.go:12-15), so an implementation outside that package cannot satisfy it. Its treatment source set is therefore exactly two created files plus runner.go.

ONE ASYMMETRY A REVIEWER SHOULD KNOW. Because this manifest declares no union, restore_baseline(randomdisagg) does not remove the other arms' 35 files if a prior arm's build left them on disk. That is harmless rather than a defect: this arm's runner.go is pristine llm-d-router plus one Register call and imports NEITHER causalsloexternality NOR leastttftjoint, so those packages fall outside the import graph of cmd/epp/main.go and the Go build never compiles them. The image is unaffected. Verified by toggle simulation, not assumed.

CORE MODIFICATION: cmd/epp/runner/runner.go, purely additive -- one fwkplugin.Register call plus a three-line comment, no existing line changed, and no new import (the disagg package is already imported at this pin). Registered StabilityAlpha: it is a control for measurement, never a deployment candidate. No extension point can replace the registration -- plugin types reach the config loader only through the process-global fwkplugin.Registry, populated in Runner.registerInTreePlugins, and the overlay switches the arm on by NAMING the type, so without it the EPP refuses to start.

THE DECISION: disaggregate(r) = U(r) < p, with U derived by hashing (seed, identity) rather than drawn from an RNG stream. Hash-derivation is a correctness requirement, not a style choice: the EPP serves requests concurrently, so a stream's position depends on arrival interleaving and would be unreplayable at a fixed seed, would need a lock on the decision path, and could answer differently on repeated calls for one request. p = 0 reproduces the simulator's `never` rule and p = 1 its `always` rule (inference-sim sim/disaggregation.go:70-74), so this arm is the interpolation between two rules the simulator already defines.

MEASURED, NOT REASONED -- THE HASH NEEDED A FINALIZER. A first implementation used FNV-1a alone and produced a realized rate of 0.541 against p = 0.5 over 200k identifiers, roughly 37 binomial standard errors off. FNV-1a avalanches poorly on inputs differing only in trailing bytes -- exactly the shape of sequential request identifiers -- so its high bits cluster, and unitInterval reads the high bits. murmur3's fmix64 finalizer fixed it: all four swept rates now track p, and two seeds at p = 0.3 disagree on 42.4 percent of requests against the theoretical 2p(1-p) = 0.42. Do not remove the finalizer as redundant, and do not substitute hash/maphash, whose per-process random seed would destroy replay.

DECLARED DEGRADATIONS R1-R5 are stated in algorithms/random_disagg.go. The two that bear on reading results: R2 -- with identityHeader empty the arm keys on Envoy's per-run RequestID, so it is exactly Bernoulli at rate p and every comparison stays valid, but two runs disaggregate DIFFERENT requests and results are not bit-replayable. R3 -- the realized rate is Binomial(n, p), so the rate itself carries sampling error on top of the usual run-to-run variance; this arm needs --replicas greater than 1 more than the deterministic arms do, and a matched-rate claim should not be made from a single cell.

VALIDATION: the Go build of cmd/epp/main.go -- the exact command Dockerfile.epp runs -- exits 0 in the applied tree; go vet exits 0; this arm's 9 tests pass; and the ENTIRE pre-existing disagg package suite passes unchanged, so no sibling decider regressed.
